subject: Request: Temporary SLA carve-out for tool-calling + structured-output failures
messages:
From: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@finguard.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finguard.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting temporary SLA carve-out for tool-call failures affecting payment pipeline

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing an increase in failures originating from the Redwood tool-calling path when our transaction enrichment tool is invoked. Failures are intermittent but spike during peak settlement windows (02:00-04:00 UTC). The downstream effect is retries on our side and occasional duplicate attempts.

We need to request a temporary SLA carve-out (latency/uptime attribution) for those specific errors while we work with your team to identify and mitigate the root cause. We are prepared to share logs and grant access to a limited subset of test traffic.

Can you confirm what information you need from us and an expected timeline for review? Our legal team also asked for written acknowledgement of the carve-out window if approved.

Thanks,
Morgan Blake
Head of Integrations, FinGuard Systems
Morgan.Blake@finguard.com

Attachments: finguard_toolcall_logs_20270322.zip

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@finguard.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting temporary SLA carve-out for tool-call failures affecting payment pipeline

Hi Morgan —

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the logs. We take incidents that impact transaction systems seriously. To proceed, we need: 

- A concise scope of the carve-out you are requesting (exact endpoints, time windows, and the specific metric you want excluded from SLA calculations).
- Representative request IDs / sample payloads so we can reproduce.
- Clarification on whether the traffic you offer us is sanitized or if we should expect live PII (we prefer redacted samples).

Our standard process is to review the evidence, run a controlled replay in a staging environment, and propose a mitigation timeline. For carve-outs, we need a signed carve-out form from legal and a proposed rollback condition (e.g., 99.5% success on replay). I've attached a draft carve-out form and cc'd Karthik for technical triage.

We aim to give an initial assessment within 48 hours once we have the samples. If you want an expedited review, let us know and we'll prioritize.

— Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Carveout_Form_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@finguard.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting temporary SLA carve-out for tool-call failures affecting payment pipeline

On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 11:05 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Morgan —
> 
> Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the logs. We take incidents that impact transaction systems seriously.

Hi all — quick technical note from triage: the attached logs indicate a higher-than-usual rate of 502/504 responses from the tool-calling layer correlated with long-tail KV cache misses. Two things to confirm from FinGuard: 1) are those replay samples hitting sequences longer than 1,024 tokens, and 2) are you using any custom tool schemas that include large binary blobs? Both would exacerbate latency.

We will stand up a controlled replay against a staging variant with cache warming enabled. If we can reproduce, mitigation paths are:
- Prefix caching for your common sequences
- Short-term increased timeouts and selective retry suppression on your integration routes
- If needed, a temporary SLA carve-out limited to the tool-calling error class and the UTC window you indicated.

Please send a sanitized sample (request IDs + payload) and a preferred carve-out window.

Cheers,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@finguard.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finguard.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting temporary SLA carve-out for tool-call failures affecting payment pipeline

Thanks Karthik —

We pulled a sanitized sample set and confirmed the sequences are typically ~800–1,100 tokens (so some exceed 1,024 occasionally). No binary blobs in the sample. I've uploaded the sanitized replay payloads to the Drive link in the carve-out form and re-attached the logs. From our side we'd request the carve-out to be limited to: 

- Error class: tool-call HTTP 5xx and structured-output validation failures only
- Time window: 02:00–04:30 UTC daily (settlement window) for up to 14 calendar days while mitigations are validated
- Rollback condition: replay in staging shows <0.5% failures for 48 hours and production error-rate drops below 0.2% in the same window

Also copying our security contact (security@finguard.com) — they asked whether Redwood will maintain an audit trail of all carve-out events and access during the investigation.

Morgan

Attachments: finguard_toolcall_logs_20270322.zip

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting temporary SLA carve-out for tool-call failures affecting payment pipeline

Thanks for the details. After a quick legal/ops check, we can provisionally approve a narrowly scoped carve-out on the terms Morgan proposed, with the following conditions: 

- Carve-out applies only to the defined error classes (tool-call 5xx and structured-output validation) and the specified UTC window.
- Duration capped at 14 days unless a joint review extends it.
- Redwood will enable audit logging for all replay runs and grant FinGuard read-only access to the incident timeline.
- Any customer-impacting incidents outside the carve-out window will be handled under standard SLA terms.

Karthik, please prioritize the staging replay with prefix cache warming and confirm the proposed rollback checks. Jasmine — I will prepare the formal carve-out amendment and have legal route the DocuSign today.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
